rules: A halal certification on the product overrides every ingredient verdict.
Any haram ingredient makes the product haram.
Otherwise any mushbooh ingredient makes the product mushbooh.
A 'vegan' label upgrades mushbooh ingredients whose vegan_label_upgrades is true to halal. It never upgrades alcohol-related ones.
Animal-derived ingredients are haram unless halal-certified; chemical transformation (istihala) does not make them halal.
An ingredient whose origin is unknown is mushbooh.

entries.name: pork
entries.rationale: Pig and all pig products are haram.

entries.name: lard
entries.rationale: Rendered pig fat.

entries.name: bacon / ham
entries.rationale: Pork products.

entries.name: pork-based sausage meats
entries.rationale: Traditionally pork; halal only when the product is halal-certified (halal versions exist).

entries.name: meat (non-halal)
entries.rationale: Meat from animals not slaughtered Islamically is haram in Hanafi fiqh; halal only with a halal certification.

entries.name: meat stock / extract
entries.rationale: Made from non-halal-slaughtered animals unless certified.

entries.name: animal fat
entries.rationale: Rendered fat from non-zabiha animals; no istihala exception.

entries.name: blood
entries.rationale: Blood is haram (Qur'an 5:3).

entries.name: bone / bone char
entries.rationale: From non-zabiha animal bones.

entries.name: collagen
entries.rationale: From pig, cattle or fish skin/bones. Halal only if marine or halal-certified.

entries.name: fish gelatin
entries.rationale: Fish are halal, so fish gelatin is halal.

entries.name: animal rennet
entries.rationale: Owner's rule: animal rennet is non-halal unless the pack has a halal stamp (follows the Saahibayn / cautious Hanafi view).
entries.contested: Imam Abu Hanifah held rennet from non-zabiha cattle permissible; some fatwas allow such cheese while recommending abstention.

entries.name: rennet (unspecified)
entries.rationale: Owner's rule (31 Oct): rennet is Haram unless the label says microbial/vegetable or the pack has a halal stamp.

entries.name: microbial / vegetable rennet
entries.rationale: Non-animal coagulant.

entries.name: pepsin
entries.rationale: Digestive enzyme usually taken from pig stomachs.

entries.name: enzymes (unspecified)
entries.rationale: Enzymes can be animal (including pork), microbial or plant-derived.

entries.name: microbial enzymes
entries.rationale: Non-animal enzymes.

entries.name: cheese
entries.rationale: Haram unless made with microbial/vegetable rennet or halal-certified (owner's rule, 31 Oct). Parmesan, Grana Padano and Pecorino are always made with animal rennet.

entries.name: whey
entries.rationale: By-product of cheese-making; follows the ruling of the rennet. Owner's rule (31 Oct): Haram unless the rennet is microbial/vegetable or the pack is halal-stamped.
entries.contested: Owner ruled Haram (31 Oct). Many Hanafi fatwas permit whey under Imam Abu Hanifah's view.

entries.name: dairy (no rennet)
entries.rationale: Milk and its products made without rennet are halal. (Rennet casein is rare.)

entries.name: egg
entries.rationale: Eggs are halal.

entries.name: honey / bee products
entries.rationale: Bee products are explicitly halal.

entries.name: insects
entries.rationale: Hanafi fiqh prohibits insects except locusts.

entries.name: fish
entries.rationale: All fish are halal in Hanafi fiqh. (Check fish sauce for added alcohol.)

entries.name: shrimp / prawn
entries.rationale: Owner ruled Halal (31 Oct): prawns are treated as fish, following Hanafi scholars such as Mufti Taqi Usmani.
entries.contested: Some Hanafi scholars call prawns makruh; owner follows the permissive view.

entries.name: shellfish / other seafood
entries.rationale: Hanafi fiqh permits only fish from the sea.
entries.contested: Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali schools permit them.

entries.name: alcoholic drinks (khamr)
entries.rationale: Intoxicating drinks are haram in any amount.

entries.name: alcohol-based extracts
entries.rationale: Extracts are usually made with ethanol. Owner ruled Haram (31 Oct); buy alcohol-free versions.
entries.contested: Darul Ifta Birmingham permits non-khamr alcohol in non-intoxicating amounts; the stricter view (owner's default) avoids it.

entries.name: flavourings
entries.rationale: Flavourings may use an alcohol carrier or contain animal-derived parts, and labels don't say which.
entries.contested: Darul Ifta Birmingham permits non-khamr alcohol in non-intoxicating amounts; the stricter view (owner's default) avoids it.

entries.name: smoke flavouring
entries.rationale: Made from burning wood.

entries.name: vinegar from alcohol
entries.rationale: Made by fermenting an alcoholic drink into vinegar.
entries.contested: Owner's rule rejects transformation (istihala), but Hanafi fiqh widely accepts wine that has turned into vinegar as pure. Owner ruled Mushbooh (31 Oct).

entries.name: vinegar (spirit / plain)
entries.rationale: Vinegar is halal; spirit vinegar comes from grain or synthetic alcohol that has fully turned into acetic acid.
entries.contested: Owner's rule rejects transformation (istihala), but Hanafi fiqh widely accepts wine that has turned into vinegar as pure. Owner ruled Mushbooh (31 Oct).

entries.name: emulsifier (unspecified)
entries.rationale: Emulsifiers such as E471 can be animal-derived; the label doesn't say which.

entries.name: glycerides / fatty acids (named)
entries.rationale: Can be made from plant oils or animal fat.

entries.name: vitamin D3
entries.rationale: Usually from lanolin (wool) or fish, which are fine, but often coated with gelatin.

entries.name: vegetable shortening / oils
entries.rationale: Plant-based fats.
